releases.body:
- **0.6.2** — OpenCode 2 context panel fixes: the V2 adapter now reads the
  model id from the store's `model.id`, so the model lookup succeeds and the
  cell grid, per-category percentages and compaction-headroom line render
  again instead of `—`; the translated messages also carry the session id, and
  the system-prompt capture anchors its freshness check to the turn's user
  message — OpenCode 2 fires the capture hook just before the assistant
  message is stamped, which previously marked every capture `(derived)`.

- **0.6.1** — Kimi Code adapter tracks the 2026-09 quota-model API change:
  usage windows now come from the `usages.limit_5h` / `limit_7d` /
  `limit_month_total` ratios (with a `limit_month_code` breakdown), and Extra
  Usage is read from the camelCase `boosterWallet` (fixed-point `BOOSTER`
  balance). The pre-2026-09 `usage` / `limits[]` / `totalQuota` /
  `booster_wallet` shapes remain as fallbacks.

The TUI plugin now loads on OpenCode 2.x. Previously `tui.json` failed with "Invalid V2 TUI plugin module", so the sidebar panel and `/usage` command silently disappeared.

**Fixed**

- The TUI entrypoint default-exports `{ id, setup, tui }`: OpenCode 2 calls `setup` (sidebar panel, `/usage` command and dialog, `session.idle` refresh via `ctx.data.on`), while OpenCode 1 still reads `tui`.
- Added `src/v2-tui.ts`, a structural mirror of the OpenCode 2 TUI context (`@opencode/plugin@2.0.20`) that adapts theme tokens, `SessionMessageInfo`, and `ui.dialog` back to the existing renderers.
- Server entrypoint unchanged since 0.5.0 (`usage_report`, low-quota warnings, prompt capture).

> Note: OpenCode 2 does not expose the resolved config to TUI plugins, so the dialog loses the compaction-reserve nuance only; token rows are unaffected.

The server plugin now loads on OpenCode 2.x. Previously it failed with "Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function".

**Fixed**

- The server entrypoint default-exports the V2 `{ id, setup }` definition, so `usage_report` and low-quota warnings work on OpenCode 2.x. The V1 `server` hook is kept, so OpenCode 1.18.29+ still loads too.

Provider HTTP plumbing is now shared and context helpers were extracted; no user-facing behavior change.

**Changed**

- Shared provider HTTP plumbing and context helpers across adapters.
